course_name_en: Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering II Engineering 2

learning_outcomes.text: Participants can distinguish between stationary, unsteady, and harmonic cases and select and apply appropriate methods and calculation rules.

Participants can calculate electrical engineering quantities in any network, select suitable measurement circuits for their measurement, and interpret, compare, and check the plausibility of the obtained results.
Participants can determine the risk to humans in case of a fault based on limit values for any arrangement, and assess and design protective measures.
Participants can draw and name simple diode rectifier circuits, explain their functionality, and analyze their output quantities.
Participants can design a transformer for given requirements, determine the quantities present in the equivalent circuit diagram, and interpret their effects on operation.
Through accompanying tutorials, subject-specific competencies are strengthened, and social competencies (including teamwork) are imparted through small group work.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the basic laws of three-phase sinusoidal circuits
Protective measures against high contact voltages
AC circuits with electrical valves (rectifier and inverter circuits)
bibliography: Busch, R.: Elektrotechnik und Elektronik-Gundlagen und Anwendungen für Ingenieure
Prechtl, A.: Vorlesungen über die Grundlagen der Elektrotechnik, Band 1 und Band 2
